panels.description: Combined physical memory held by the VoltDB processes across all nodes. Watch it grow with your data so you can add capacity before nodes approach their limits.
panels.title: Cluster RSS total

panels.description: Total database records in memory across the cluster.
panels.title: Cluster tuple count

panels.description: Combined Java heap in use across all nodes - the cluster-wide counterpart of the per-node heap panels below. Rising heap usually tracks growing data and workload; compare it with the per-node view to see whether growth is spread evenly.
panels.title: Java heap used (cluster)

panels.description: The most memory-stressed server, shown as a percentage of its configured memory limit. VoltDB pauses the database if a server reaches 100% of this limit.
panels.title: Max RSS vs mem limit

panels.description: Physical memory held by the VoltDB process on each node. Compare nodes to spot one growing faster than the rest or approaching its memory limit.
panels.title: RSS size

panels.description: How much of each server's memory VoltDB is using, as a percentage.
panels.title: % of available memory used

panels.description: Each server's memory in use compared with its configured memory limit. VoltDB pauses the database if usage reaches the limit.
panels.title: Memory limit vs RSS

panels.description: How much of the Java heap each node is using against the maximum it is allowed to grow to. A node whose used heap stays close to its max is under memory pressure and may see longer pauses or run out of heap.
panels.title: Java heap used vs max

panels.description: Memory each node holds for table rows: the data line is what the rows actually occupy, while allocated also includes free space reserved for growth and left behind by deletes. A widening gap between the two indicates fragmentation that compaction can reclaim.
panels.title: Tuple data / allocated

panels.description: Memory each node uses for larger text, binary, and geospatial column values that are stored outside the main row storage. It grows as you store more or longer values of these types.
panels.title: String memory

panels.description: Memory each node uses to hold table indexes. It grows with row count and with the number and width of your indexes, adding to a node's footprint separately from the row data itself.
panels.title: Index memory

panels.description: Memory each node uses for internal work other than table rows, indexes, and large string values, such as query execution and temporary results. Useful for explaining the part of a node's footprint not accounted for by stored data.
panels.title: Pooled memory

panels.description: Number of table rows held in memory on each node. Compare nodes to confirm data is spread evenly and to watch overall growth over time.
panels.title: Tuple count

panels.description: Trend of the combined physical memory held by the VoltDB processes across all nodes - the same measurement as the 'Cluster RSS total' tile above, over time. Watch it grow with your data so you can add capacity before nodes approach their limits.
panels.title: Cluster RSS total (over time)

panels.description: Time each node spends in the short, frequent garbage collections that reclaim recently allocated Java memory. Occasional small values are normal; sustained high values mean the node is pausing often to free memory.
panels.title: New Gen GC Time

panels.description: How often each node runs the short garbage collections that reclaim recently allocated Java memory. A rising rate points to heavy memory churn that can add latency.
panels.title: New Gen GC Count

panels.description: Time each node spends in the heavier garbage collections that reclaim long-lived Java memory. These can cause longer pauses, so sustained or rising values are worth investigating as a sign of memory pressure.
panels.title: Old Gen GC Time

panels.description: How often each node runs the heavier garbage collections that reclaim long-lived Java memory. Frequent runs usually indicate the heap is filling up and the node is under memory pressure.
panels.title: Old Gen GC Count
